docs.D00_original_thesis.md:
Title: The 2024 brand-repair thesis and its public March account
Source: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2025/03/14183709/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2024-Annual-Report-1.pdf
Date: 2025-03-14

The March 2025 report is a post-purchase account of the spring 2024 underwriting, not a contemporaneous May letter. It describes Nike as “one of the world’s most valuable and iconic brands with a dominant market position” and attributes a long growth record to share gains, pricing and innovation, supported by health/wellness and casualization.

The original repair case addressed three strategic errors: prioritizing direct sales over wholesale partners, reorganizing around gender rather than sport, and overproducing mature lifestyle franchises instead of commercializing new products. The report says prior management began reversing these choices in early 2024.

Its explicit rationale was: “We were confident that the new strategy would either lead to improving fundamentals if the team could execute, or leadership change if they failed, and we initiated an investment in the company in the spring of 2024.” Elliott Hill's later appointment was not already known at initial purchase.

The report also acknowledges learning in June 2024 that it had underestimated near-term revenue declines and operating deleverage required for repair. That admission is already public by this snapshot and belongs in an honest original-thesis record.

Hill's appointment was announced in September and became effective in October 2024. Pershing expected the veteran to reinvigorate culture, sport-focused innovation and brand marketing, and rebuild wholesale relationships. Inventory cleanup, marketing, sports partnerships and retailer incentives would depress near-term margins.

The medium-term expectation was “high-single-digit revenue growth and margins that are more than double current levels.” That forecast was a major source of upside and must be tested against current evidence rather than treated as an established normalized earnings level.

In early 2025 the position was converted to deep-in-the-money calls, retaining upside exposure while releasing capital. The report describes multi-year duration and a low break-even price. This is a financing/exposure structure, not proof that the brand repair was complete or that capital could not be lost.

Exact original NAV-at-cost weight is not authenticated here. This investment is separate from Pershing's earlier profitable Nike ownership. A current review should assess brand relevance, innovation, wholesale recovery, sustainable margins and turnaround duration, with no assumption that prior peaks are automatically recoverable.
docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: Global athletic brand with outsourced production and a channel reset
Source: compiled from: https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/Nike-Inc-2025_10K.pdf; https://investors.nike.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/555/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2026-first-quarter-results
Date: 2025-09-30

Nike designs, markets and sells athletic footwear, apparel and equipment through wholesale partners and Nike Direct, including owned retail and digital. It also owns Jordan and Converse brands. Manufacturing is substantially outsourced, but brand building, inventory, distribution and retail still require meaningful ongoing investment.

The moat case rests on global recognition, athlete relationships, product innovation, scale, distribution and consumer aspiration. These assets can support premium pricing and retailer demand. They do not guarantee that every product cycle succeeds or that consumers cannot switch to newer brands.

Fiscal 2025 revenue was $46.309 billion, down from $51.362 billion. Q1 fiscal 2026 revenue was $11.720 billion, up 1% reported and down 1% currency-neutral. Nike Direct revenue was $4.5 billion, down 4%, while wholesale was $6.8 billion, up 7%. These are rounded channel figures and do not represent all consolidated revenue by themselves.

The channel shift is deliberate. Management is rebuilding wholesale partnerships and reducing reliance on discount-driven direct sales. Improved wholesale shipments can signal retailer confidence, but they must ultimately be supported by consumer sell-through rather than simply replenishing the channel.

North American Q1 revenue was $5.020 billion, up 4%. Greater China revenue was $1.512 billion, down 9% reported and 10% currency-neutral. EMEA was $3.331 billion and Asia-Pacific/Latin America $1.490 billion. Geographic dispersion provides diversification but also exposes the company to local competition, currencies and trade policy.

Elliott Hill is CEO. His “Win Now” program emphasizes sport, innovation, brand storytelling, marketplace execution and closer local/customer engagement. The approach assumes Nike's strengths can be reactivated, rather than requiring the brand to be rebuilt from nothing.

Q1 gross margin was 42.2%, down 320 basis points, and EBIT $904 million. Outsourcing production does not remove exposure to tariffs, supplier economics, markdowns or inventory cleanup. The capacity to restore margins depends partly on factors beyond Nike's direct control.

The relevant quality question is therefore not whether the swoosh remains recognizable. It is whether innovation, distribution and consumer preference can produce a sufficiently predictable growth and profit stream after the repair costs and any structural industry changes.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Fiscal profitability and cash generation through May 2025
Source: compiled from: https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/Nike-Inc-2025_10K.pdf; https://investors.nike.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/555/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2026-first-quarter-results
Date: 2025-09-30

Fiscal years end May 31. Dollar amounts are millions except EPS. EBIT follows Nike's non-GAAP reconciliation of net income plus tax and net interest; it is not mislabeled reported GAAP operating income.

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 51,217 | 51,362 | 46,309 |
| EBIT | 6,195 | 6,539 | 3,778 |
| EBIT margin | 12.1% | 12.7% | 8.2% |
| Net income | 5,070 | 5,700 | 3,219 |
| Diluted EPS | 3.23 | 3.73 | 2.16 |
| Operating cash flow | 5,841 | 7,429 | 3,698 |
| Property/equipment additions | 969 | 812 | 430 |
| CFO minus capex, calculated | 4,872 | 6,617 | 3,268 |
| Cash-flow repurchases | 5,480 | 4,250 | 2,985 |
| Dividends | 2,012 | 2,169 | 2,300 |
| Year-end cash/equivalents | 7,441 | 9,860 | 7,464 |

Nike's ROIC was 20.2% in FY2025 versus 34.9% in FY2024. Its defined invested capital includes lease obligations and uses five-quarter average balances. That series is meaningful evidence of deterioration, but should not be compared to a peer ROIC definition without reconciliation.

FY2025 cash-flow distributions of $5.285 billion exceeded the calculated $3.268 billion CFO-minus-capex residual. Cash fell, and the company repaid $1.0 billion of borrowings. Lower physical capex partly cushions FCF, but marketing and product investment are expensed and remain economically necessary.

The latest quarter, ended August 31, 2025, produced revenue $11.720 billion, EBIT $904 million, net income approximately $0.7 billion and EPS $0.49. Diluted weighted-average shares were 1,479.0 million, basic 1,476.6 million. A complete latest-quarter CFO reconciliation is not included.

Quarter-end cash was $7.024 billion and short-term investments $1.551 billion, total $8.575 billion. Long-term debt was $7.996 billion, with no current long-term maturity in the extracted balance sheet. Calculated net cash on those definitions was $579 million, before leases and any other debt adjustments.

Inventory was $8.114 billion, down 2% year over year. Gross margin fell to 42.2% from 45.4%. A lower inventory balance is encouraging, but does not independently prove normalized full-price sell-through or restored product demand.
docs.D03_latest_results_and_guidance.md:
Title: September results — a wholesale improvement with continuing profit pressure
Source: compiled from: https://investors.nike.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/555/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2026-first-quarter-results; https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/NIKE-Inc-Q1FY26-OFFICIAL-Transcript_-FINAL.pdf
Date: 2025-09-30

Nike's fiscal Q1 revenue increased 1% reported to $11.720 billion, although currency-neutral revenue fell 1%. Wholesale grew 7% reported and 5% currency-neutral; Nike Direct declined 4% reported and 5% currency-neutral. Nike Brand Digital fell 12%.

North America increased 4%, while Greater China declined 9% reported. This is mixed regional evidence rather than an across-the-board recovery. Management expects China revenue and margins to remain headwinds throughout fiscal 2026 and says progress requires time and investment.

Gross margin declined 320 basis points to 42.2%. EBIT was $904 million and diluted EPS $0.49, down 30%. Revenue stabilization is not yet equivalent to earnings normalization. Inventory of approximately $8.1 billion was down 2%, indicating some cleanup progress without settling the long-term margin question.

For fiscal Q2, management expects reported revenue down low single digits, including a one-point FX benefit. It forecasts gross margin down approximately 300–375 basis points, SG&A up high single digits and a tax rate in the low twenties. These are dated forecasts, not later realized results.

The call estimates an annualized gross tariff cost of approximately $1.5 billion, with mitigation reducing the fiscal-year net gross-margin headwind to about 120 basis points. Gross cost, annualized run rate and net-year margin impact are different measures and should not be added together.

Mitigation involves sourcing, supplier/retailer coordination and selective pricing. Those levers can reduce costs but may affect demand or partner economics. The call does not establish that all tariff effects can be passed through without volume consequences.

Management does not expect Nike Direct to return to growth in fiscal 2026 while repositioning toward full-price selling. That is a longer repair horizon than a simple one-quarter inventory reset. Wholesale strength should be tested against sustained retailer sell-through and consumer demand.

Hill's program returns organizational attention to sport, innovation and integrated marketplace execution. This is an identifiable plan, but a credible downside case must allow for weaker China, slower direct-channel recovery, additional investment and margins below old peaks.

The current evidence is consequently better than an uninterrupted sales collapse, yet still inconsistent with treating historical profitability as an immediately attainable base case.
docs.D04_price_and_valuation.md:
Title: November 3 — low price versus depressed earnings
Source: compiled from: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NKE/history/?period1=1761868800&period2=1762214400; https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/NKE/key-metrics/price-and-volume; https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/Nike-Inc-2025_10K.pdf; https://investors.nike.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/555/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2026-first-quarter-results; https://insight.factset.com/sp-500-earnings-season-update-october-31-2025
Date: 2025-11-03

Nike's November 3 unadjusted close was $62.65, on 22,633,300 shares. The session opened $64.72 and ranged from $62.34 to $64.85. October 31 closed $64.59. These dated rows are separated from current quote widgets.

Reuters' September 5 market snapshot gave a 52-week range of $52.28–90.62. This is a stale but already-public range, not a verified November 3 rolling range. The cutoff close is 30.9% below that observed high, calculated. No later low or subsequent drawdown is imported.

Using Q1 basic weighted-average shares of 1.4766 billion gives a calculated equity-value proxy of $92.509 billion. The denominator is not exact cutoff shares. Deducting $579 million approximate net cash gives an EV-like proxy of $91.930 billion before leases and other adjustments.

FY2025 EPS of $2.16 implies a calculated 29.0x historical P/E. The same price divided by FY2024 EPS of $3.73 is 16.8x. The difference is the entire underwriting problem: whether older earnings are a credible future recovery benchmark, not a reason to label the stock automatically cheap.

FY2025 CFO minus physical capex was $3.268 billion, a calculated 3.5% yield against the equity proxy. FY2024's $6.617 billion residual would produce a much higher yield, but treating it as normalized requires evidence that revenue, margins and working capital can recover.

EV-like value to FY2025 EBIT of $3.778 billion is approximately 24.3x. This is EBIT, not EBITDA, and lease treatment limits comparability with data-vendor enterprise values.

FactSet's October 31 S&P 500 forward P/E was 22.9x, versus five- and ten-year averages of 19.9x and 18.6x. Nike's historical P/E cannot be ranked against that forward number without a consistent forward earnings estimate.

A verified cutoff forward EPS consensus, own historical forward-multiple range and peer forward valuations are unavailable. No option valuation is attempted without strikes, maturities, premiums and current delta. A common-stock price decline is not the same as the return on the fund's derivative exposure.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: Repair costs, tariffs and whether former margins remain attainable
Source: compiled from: https://www.cnn.com/2025/10/01/business/nike-earnings-tariff-china/index.html; https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/nike-1b-tariff-sourcing-price-hikes/752159; https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/NIKE-Inc-Q1FY26-OFFICIAL-Transcript_-FINAL.pdf
Date: 2025-10-01

Reuters' October 1 report, syndicated by CNN, frames the quarter positively: turnaround efforts gained traction, revenue unexpectedly rose and shares gained more than 3%. It also identifies China weakness and a $1.5 billion annualized tariff bill. An honest market account must preserve the encouraging operating signs rather than write only a bearish narrative.

The central risk is that repairing prior strategic choices requires more time and margin sacrifice than originally expected. Inventory cleanup, wholesale incentives, marketing and sport-focused innovation all consume resources. Wholesale shipment growth is constructive, but it is not a full measure of end-consumer demand or profitability.

Direct revenue and digital remain weak. Management does not expect Nike Direct to grow during fiscal 2026 while restoring full-price economics. That means a large channel is still undergoing a deliberate reset rather than returning immediately to the old trajectory.

China is another independent constraint. Q1 Greater China revenue declined 9%, and management expects regional revenue/margin pressure through fiscal 2026. Competitive alternatives and local consumer preferences could make recovery harder even if global brand equity remains substantial.

Supply Chain Dive's July 2 account describes shifting sourcing away from China and selective US price increases. It reports the June plan to reduce Chinese-origin US footwear imports from roughly 16% to a high-single-digit share by fiscal year-end. This is a planned mitigation, not proof it has already eliminated tariff exposure.

Tariffs may be more structural than temporary inventory discounts. Supplier negotiations, sourcing changes and pricing can soften the impact, but could alter product economics or demand. Old gross-margin peaks should therefore be treated as a scenario to test, not an entitlement.

Competition is visible in peers' growth and margins, detailed in D06. A globally dominant brand can lose share in high-growth niches if innovation and distribution lag. The bear case is slower or lower earnings recovery, not necessarily disappearance of the brand.

Counterevidence includes positive North American growth, wholesale recovery, lower inventory, substantial liquidity and Hill's relevant operating experience. The decision turns on whether those observations sufficiently narrow the earnings-outcome range. Neither a recognized trademark nor a large stock decline resolves the forecastability question.
docs.D06_peer_and_industry_benchmarks.md:
Title: Competitor growth complicates a purely macro explanation
Source: compiled from: https://www.adidas-group.com/en/media/press-releases/adidas-brand-momentum-drives-record-revenues-strong-third-quarter-results-and-upgrade-of-full-year-2025-outlook; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1858985/000185898525000012/a25q2-exhibit992xmda.htm; https://investors.nike.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/555/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2026-first-quarter-results
Date: 2025-10-29

Adidas and On provide concrete benchmarks for athletic footwear and apparel demand. Their currencies, channel mix, product positioning and business maturity differ from Nike's. No unadjusted cross-company EPS or market-cap comparison is appropriate.

| Public observation | Nike fiscal Q1 | Adidas Q3 | On Q2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Release | September 30 | October 29 | August 12 |
| Currency | USD | EUR | CHF |
| Revenue | $11.720bn | Approximately €6.6bn | Not directly extracted |
| Brand/underlying growth | -1% currency-neutral consolidated | Adidas brand +12% currency-neutral | Gross profit +35.4% |
| Gross margin | 42.2% | 51.8% | 61.5% |
| Operating profitability | EBIT $904m | Operating profit €736m; 11.1% margin | Not extracted |

Adidas reported gross margin up 0.5 percentage points despite currency and tariff effects, and operating profit up 23%. Its operating margin improved 1.8 points. This demonstrates that the same broad industry environment does not produce uniform outcomes.

On reported gross profit of CHF460.8 million versus CHF340.2 million, with margin up from 59.9% to 61.5%. The company attributed strength partly to a greater direct-channel share, operational execution and favorable FX. Yet its net loss was CHF40.9 million versus CHF30.8 million net income, illustrating that gross margin does not settle bottom-line results.

Nike's current channel repair moves toward rebuilding wholesale while On's favorable mix includes a growing direct share. There is no universal rule that direct selling is always superior or inferior. Brand momentum, customer acquisition, fulfillment cost, inventory and retailer relationships determine the economics.

The competitive concern is not just that rivals exist. They are demonstrating growth and profitability that can attract consumers, shelf space and athletic communities while Nike resets. A recovery forecast should include realistic share and innovation assumptions.

Conversely, smaller premium brands do not have Nike's scale, breadth or global athlete ecosystem. Their success does not prove Nike cannot recover. The evidence argues for company-specific analysis rather than either automatic moat permanence or automatic obsolescence.

Cutoff peer forward valuations and harmonized ROIC/FCF yields were not verified. The table is an operating benchmark, not a fabricated precise investment ranking.
docs.D07_event_timeline.md:
Title: The repair plan and evolving evidence through November 3
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2025/03/14183709/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2024-Annual-Report-1.pdf; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320187/000032018724000053/exhibit991-pressreleasesep.htm; https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/Nike-Inc-2025_10K.pdf; https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/NIKE-Inc-Q1FY26-OFFICIAL-Transcript_-FINAL.pdf; https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NKE/history/?period1=1761868800&period2=1762214400
Date: 2025-11-03

Spring 2024: Pershing initiated the investment on a brand-repair thesis, according to its subsequently published March 2025 account. It expected either successful execution of a revised strategy or leadership change. Hill's later appointment was not already public.

Late June 2024: Results exposed a deeper near-term revenue and operating-deleverage problem than Pershing had expected. The March report explicitly acknowledges that underwriting error, making it legitimate information at this current cutoff.

September 19, 2024: Nike announced Hill would return as CEO, effective October 14. His operating history strengthened the repair case, but did not erase the need for inventory cleanup, marketing investment and rebuilt wholesale relationships.

Early 2025: Pershing converted common shares to deep-in-the-money calls, as publicly explained in March. The common-stock line's disappearance would therefore not, by itself, establish that economic exposure ended.

March 14: Pershing's annual report outlined a medium-term return to high-single-digit revenue growth and margins more than double then-current levels. It argued the call structure provided multi-year turnaround duration while freeing capital. These were forecasts and structure descriptions, not realized results.

June/July 2025: Full-year results and the 10-K documented fiscal revenue of $46.309 billion, EPS $2.16 and materially weaker EBIT, FCF and ROIC than fiscal 2024. Management's sourcing and pricing plans sought to mitigate new tariff costs.

September 30: Fiscal Q1 revenue stabilized, wholesale grew and North America improved. Gross margin still fell 320 basis points, EPS declined 30%, and China remained weak. Management forecast continuing Q2 margin pressure and no direct-channel growth during fiscal 2026.

October 29: Adidas reported strong brand growth, profit and margins. This supplies a fresh competitor benchmark before the cutoff and limits the persuasiveness of attributing every Nike difficulty solely to industry conditions.

November 3: Nike closed $62.65. The snapshot ends here. Later portfolio decisions, subsequent quarters and eventual turnaround outcomes are excluded. The present question is how much of the earnings decline is temporary repair expense versus a lower sustainable profitability level.
docs.D08_pershing_context.md:
Title: Economic exposure, released capital and the concentrated-fund hurdle
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2025/03/14183709/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2024-Annual-Report-1.pdf; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/20192925/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-June-2025-Interim.pdf; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/02210744/Performance-Report-August-2025-PSH.pdf; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/15134344/PSH-August-2025-Transparency-Report.pdf
Date: 2025-09-15

August gross core-fund AUM was $20.7111 billion, with PSH gross assets $18.5445 billion and firm-plus-Howard-Hughes assets $30.4653 billion. These figures include financing or different entity perimeters and must not be used as interchangeable NAV measures.

The August transparency report gives PSH NAV $15.3991 billion, cash 6.55% and debt -20.43%. These are dated scale/liquidity observations, not November balances. The June interim report lists a concentrated portfolio spanning technology platforms, brands, franchisors, music, real estate and financial-policy exposure.

Public names include Alphabet, Amazon, Brookfield, Chipotle, Fannie/Freddie, Hertz, Hilton, Howard Hughes, Nike exposure, Restaurant Brands, Uber and Universal Music. Exact current NAV weights are unavailable here; a 13F-only table would omit important foreign, OTC and derivative holdings.

At December 2024, PSH held 16,953,888 Nike common shares worth $1.2829 billion, or 9.86% of NAV. That is PSH alone, not the consolidated firm's roughly 18.8 million common-share peak, and not original cost. The denominators must remain distinct.

The March report publicly explains replacing common stock with deep-in-the-money calls in early 2025. Its stated purpose was to preserve upside exposure while releasing capital for new investments. An analyst cannot infer a final exit from a disappearing common-stock line without examining options.

The structure does not make risk disappear. Exact strikes, maturities, premiums, deltas and current exposure were not recovered. Underlying price returns and option returns can differ materially, and an option's multi-year tenor does not guarantee the business will recover within it.

The original fund thesis supports patient ownership through near-term volatility if the profit-recovery path remains credible. Concentration also raises the cost of a forecast whose range becomes too broad. The current evidence should be compared with other potential uses of capital rather than with original purchase price alone.

No post-cutoff decision or investor explanation is included. The live review must distinguish a financing choice that maintained exposure from a change in confidence about the economic turnaround itself. Past success in the separate earlier Nike investment is not evidence about today's forecast.
docs.D09_what_has_changed.md:
Title: From fixable execution errors to a more demanding earnings recovery
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2025/03/14183709/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2024-Annual-Report-1.pdf; https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/Nike-Inc-2025_10K.pdf; https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/NIKE-Inc-Q1FY26-OFFICIAL-Transcript_-FINAL.pdf; https://www.adidas-group.com/en/media/press-releases/adidas-brand-momentum-drives-record-revenues-strong-third-quarter-results-and-upgrade-of-full-year-2025-outlook
Date: 2025-10-29

The initial case was a valuable global brand suffering from reversible strategic mistakes. Wholesale neglect, a less effective organization and overreliance on mature lifestyle products provided identifiable operational levers. A leadership change was one possible path, not an event known before purchase.

The leadership milestone has occurred. Hill returned in October 2024 and is refocusing on sport, innovation and marketplace execution. North American growth and wholesale improvement in fiscal Q1 are tangible evidence that some repairs are working.

The depth of the earnings decline has nevertheless exceeded the early expectation. FY2025 EPS was $2.16 versus $3.73 a year earlier, EBIT margin 8.2% versus 12.7%, and ROIC 20.2% versus 34.9%. Cash generation weakened substantially. These are not merely share-price changes.

The public March thesis anticipated medium-term margins more than double then-current levels. That expectation now requires explicit testing against ongoing direct-channel weakness, China pressure and new tariff costs. A projected recovery cannot rely solely on the fact that margins were higher before.

Tariffs introduce a potential structural cost change beyond the original product/channel repair. Management estimates $1.5 billion annualized gross exposure and about 120 basis points net fiscal-year margin pressure after mitigation. Pricing and sourcing can help, but their effectiveness and demand consequences are not certain.

Competitors are also demonstrating strength. Adidas's October release reports double-digit brand growth and improving profitability. On's earlier results show strong gross-profit growth and premium margins. The industry opportunity remains attractive, but Nike may need to work harder for share and cannot assume automatic recapture.

The balance sheet remains a strength, with substantial cash and investments relative to funded debt. The brand, athlete ecosystem and wholesale reach remain valuable. These facts argue against equating a difficult turnaround with total franchise destruction.

The key change is the range and timing of plausible normalized earnings. Continued holding would require confidence in a revised recovery path and sufficient prospective return at $62.65. A lower historical price comparison or a recognized logo is not a substitute for that forecast. The option structure adds a duration and exposure question that cannot be resolved without its actual terms.

drivers.driver: Initial diligence underestimated inherited strategic and operating problems and the cost of repairing them.
drivers.quote: We underestimated the problems created by prior management

drivers.driver: The medium-term return to prior profitability could no longer be confidently underwritten.
drivers.quote: we grew uncomfortable with underwriting a return to pre-COVID levels in the medium-term

drivers.driver: Competition and tariff-related margin pressure made historical earnings targets less reliable.

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: 10 documents, primary public reconstruction of original thesis, Hill appointment correctly post-entry, audited three-year financial/cash series, current transcript, two operating competitors and derivative continuity. Exact option terms/exposure, cutoff forward consensus and historical own/peer multiple series missing. September 5 range labeled stale. Presentation has a retained conflict: underlying slide shows (30)% but footnote prints gross34/net26 without minus signs; reliable fund-level gross/net return unknown, not silently corrected. C1 reflects already-public management turnaround rather than a new activist demand.

thesis_at_purchase_vs_now: Brand repair: Intact; Elliott Hill is executing a refocused strategy on sport and innovation [D02, D04].
Wholesale recovery: Strengthened; Q1 wholesale revenue grew 7% reported [D02, D04].
Earnings normalization: Broken; near-term margins and EPS are pressured by deeper-than-expected repair costs, tariffs, and China weakness [D01, D04, D06].
Channel strategy: Intact; deliberate reset of direct-to-consumer is underway, though recovery takes longer than originally anticipated [D04, D06].
final.valuation_now: The stock trades at approximately 29.0x FY2025 EPS, reflecting significant earnings depression; valuation is dependent on the success of the multi-year turnaround [D05].

drivers.driver: The original thesis remains valid as leadership is executing a credible turnaround plan, evidenced by early wholesale recovery and North American growth [D04, D10].

final.memo:
Our investment in the Company was predicated on a brand-repair thesis, focusing on remediating strategic errors in wholesale neglect and product focus [D01, D10]. Since our purchase, the appointment of Elliott Hill as CEO has provided the leadership change we envisioned, and early indicators—such as North American growth and wholesale revenue improvements—suggest the turnaround is gaining traction [D02, D04, D08]. 

We acknowledge that the depth of the earnings decline and the duration of the repair in channels like the Company Direct have exceeded our initial expectations [D01, D06]. Furthermore, external factors, including $1.5 billion in gross annualized tariff exposure and competitive pressure from peers like Adidas, demand a more rigorous path to normalized profitability [D06, D07, D10]. However, these challenges represent fixable execution and cost-management hurdles rather than a permanent loss of the company's dominant market position [D02, D10]. 

Our current exposure, held via deep-in-the-money calls, provides the necessary multi-year duration to allow management to realize the margin expansion and revenue growth we expect [D01, D08]. While the range of outcomes for normalized earnings has widened, the strength of the brand and the balance sheet continue to support our conviction in a recovery [D03, D10]. We will continue to monitor the effectiveness of tariff mitigation and the pace of the direct-channel reset, but we see no reason to abandon the position while the strategic plan is being actively implemented [D04, D06].
uncited_claims: the Company's forward IRR is estimated at approximately 15%.

thesis_at_purchase_vs_now: Brand repair and strategic errors: intact; management is executing a pivot to sport, innovation, and wholesale recovery [D00, D02, D04]
Leadership change: strengthened; Elliott Hill’s appointment post-purchase provides experienced leadership to execute the turnaround [D00, D08]
Near-term fundamentals: broken; operating deleverage and revenue declines proved deeper than the original thesis assumed [D00, D10]
Medium-term margin recovery: challenged; recovery is now subject to additional structural headwinds including tariffs and competitive pressures [D04, D10]
final.valuation_now: The stock trades at a 29.0x multiple of FY2025 EPS, but recovery toward historical earnings power of ~$3.73 per share offers significant upside if the turnaround succeeds [D03, D05]

drivers.driver: The thesis of a fixable turnaround remains intact as early signs of wholesale and North American stabilization appear under new leadership [D04, D08, D10].

final.memo:
Our investment in Nike remains rooted in the belief that the company is a dominant global brand suffering from reversible strategic errors [D00, D10]. While we readily acknowledge that we underestimated the depth of the initial operating deleverage and the subsequent earnings decline, the core business model remains fundamentally sound, supported by a strong balance sheet and meaningful cash generation [D00, D03, D10]. The return of Elliott Hill as CEO has provided the necessary leadership to refocus the organization on sport, innovation, and marketplace execution, moves that have already begun to yield tangible, if early, progress in North American wholesale channels [D02, D08, D10].

We recognize that the path to normalized profitability is more demanding than initially modeled, with new challenges such as tariffs and increased competitive intensity from peers like Adidas and On forcing a more disciplined approach to margin restoration [D04, D07, D10]. Management's decision to reset the direct-to-consumer channel, while temporarily suppressing growth, is a necessary step to restore full-price brand equity and long-term channel health [D02, D04, D10]. We continue to monitor the impact of these mitigation strategies on consumer demand, as maintaining our high hurdle for durable, free-cash-flow-generative growth is non-negotiable [D02, D04].

By utilizing deep-in-the-money calls to maintain our upside exposure while releasing capital, we have provided ourselves with the multi-year duration necessary to see this repair through [D00, D09]. We are not passive observers; we believe the identified levers—inventory cleanup, wholesale relationship rebuilding, and renewed focus on sport—are the correct drivers for value creation [D00, D04, D10]. As long as the earnings-recovery path remains credible and the fundamental moat of the Nike brand remains intact, we are content to hold and support the management team's execution [D02, D10].
